conclusion.HIGH: Based on the screening, your scabies risk is high. There are key symptoms that need to be checked by a health worker soon.
conclusion.MODERATE: There are some signs that need attention. It may not be scabies, but it is best to stay alert and keep good hygiene.
conclusion.LOW: Based on this screening, your scabies risk is low. No need to worry too much, but keep up your hygiene habits.

perception.HIGH: We understand this might feel worrying. But with the right care, scabies can be treated and cured.
perception.MODERATE: No need to panic. What matters is that you are aware and can start taking better care of your hygiene.
perception.LOW: Great that you care about your skin health! Keep up the clean habits you already have.

recommendation.HIGH:
See a health cadre or doctor as soon as possible
Do not share towels, combs, or other personal items
Wash bed sheets and pillowcases with hot water
Dry your mattress and pillows under sunlight
Tell your roommates to get checked too
recommendation.MODERATE:
Keep your personal and sleeping area clean
Do not share towels or clothes with others
Change bed sheets at least once a week
If itching does not improve in 3 days, see a health cadre or doctor
recommendation.LOW:
Keep up daily personal hygiene
Do not share personal items like towels and combs
Change clothes and bed sheets regularly

suggestion.HIGH: Do not delay getting checked. The sooner it is treated, the sooner you will recover. If needed, ask your roommates to get checked too.
suggestion.MODERATE: Watch if the itching gets worse or appears in new areas. If so, see a health cadre right away.
suggestion.LOW: Keep up your hygiene and watch for any skin changes. If unusual itching appears later, do not hesitate to screen again.

cara.title: How to Use SICAPS
cara.step1Desc: Name, age, and education level. Just a moment.
cara.step2Desc: Answer the questions by text or voice. Relax, just like chatting.
cara.step3Desc: Capi gives a risk score and treatment advice that fits you.
cara.noteDesc: SICAPS is an initial screening tool, not a replacement for a doctor's examination. If your result is at risk, please see a health worker soon.
